summary: HIVE Autonomy scores 32/100 — well below the 50 threshold. The company appears to be building autonomous drone/swarm technology, but shows limited evidence across all five thesis pillars: team lacks visible domain depth or prior exits; defensibility is unclear with no disclosed IP or technical moat; product maturity is uncertain with no public demo or customer references; market timing is plausible (defense/logistics autonomy) but entry strategy is opaque; traction appears pre-revenue with no announced pilots, contracts, or funding. At this stage there is insufficient signal to justify a meeting.
rationale: Team: No public profiles showing deep robotics/autonomy experience or prior venture outcomes. Defensibility: No patents, technical publications, or architecture details disclosed — hard to assess moat vs. incumbents (Shield AI, Anduril, Skydio) or open-source stacks (PX4/ArduPilot). Product: Website describes vision but no video, spec sheet, or developer docs; unclear if hardware, software, or both. Market & Why-Now: Autonomy tailwinds exist (DoD Replicator, last-mile logistics), but go-to-market (dual-use? direct gov? platform play?) is undefined. Traction/Freshness: No announced pilots, LOIs, SBIRs, or fundraising; site copyright 2024 suggests very early stage. Overall: Too many unknowns; score reflects high uncertainty across every dimension.
changeMyMind: Publishes technical whitepaper or demo video showing swarm coordination in GPS-denied environments with measurable metrics (latency, scale, reliability)
Announces first paid pilot or SBIR Phase II with a named DoD/logistics partner and discloses contract value
Adds a founding team member with prior autonomy shipping experience (e.g., ex-Shield AI, Skydio, Waymo, or NASA JPL) and files 2+ core patents
